- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.4.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast slightly if sentiment remains low or shows early recovery.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior day) — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if model forecasts 3–5 days ahead, it often overestimates by 2–4% — apply a 1–2% downward correction for 3–5 day horizons.
- High sentiment + high price history → model tends to overreact — cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day high if sentiment > 0.6.
- Low sentiment + low price history → model underreacts — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment < 0.3 and price < 70.00.
